The doors of Cadillac One opened as security personnel scanned the surroundings one final time. President Krump stepped out first, adjusting his suit before gesturing toward the entrance. Standing at the top of the steps was Vice President Morgan Fring Gustavo, with senior advisors and White House officials.

[b]Krump[/b]
 Meet my Vice President, Morgan Fring Gustavo.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 Nice to meet you, Mr. President. Were honored to have you here at the White House.

Gustavo extended his hand with a firm, diplomatic smile. After the greeting, he stepped slightly aside and gestured toward the entrance.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 If youd both follow me, weve prepared the West Wing conference chamber. We can continue the meeting in a more secure and private area.

Inside the White House

The group moved through the corridors of the White House, passing portraits of former leaders and guarded intersections staffed with USO security. Inside, the conference room was already prepared. A large oval table sat at the center, equipped with screen displays, folders of briefing documents, and small national flags representing both nations. Senior officials from economic, defense, and intelligence departments were seated and stood upon the presidents arrival.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 Gentlemen, thank you all for assembling. Todays closed door session will focus on border security cooperation and economic expansion.

He paused, activating the screen behind him displaying data charts and regional maps.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 Our intelligence indicates increasing cross border movement tied to organized criminal networks. We believe coordinated enforcement and intelligence sharing will be critical moving forward.

He turned slightly toward Krump.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 Mr. President, the floor is yours to outline the administrations expectations.

Krump stepped forward, placing both hands on the table as the room quieted.

[b]Krump[/b]
 As weve discussed earlier, this is no longer a minor issue, its a growing security concern. Our priority is clear, stability within our borders and accountability beyond them.
He tapped a remote, shifting the display to a series of incident reports and trafficking routes.

[b]Krump[/b]
 We are proposing a joint task force between our Federal Bureau of Security Intelligence and your national enforcement agencies. Shared databases, coordinated raids, and stricter border enforcement protocols.

He glanced briefly around the room, ensuring every official was engaged.

[b]Krump[/b]
 In addition, we expect stronger action against the criminal networks exporting narcotics and illegal immigration into our territory.

He stepped back, allowing the economic advisors to prepare their materials. Gustavo nodded toward a group of analysts seated along the right side of the table.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 Moving to economic cooperation, our administration sees an opportunity in market integration.

A presentation appeared showing projected growth curves and trade routes.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 We are proposing the expansion of USO based technology firms and insurance corporations into New Westmore under a regulated free-market agreement. In return, we aim to establish joint aviation partnerships to boost tourism and commercial travel.

He folded his hands calmly.

[b]Gustavo[/b]
 We focus on how both the New Westmore and USO form a long term economic alignment.

[b]Krump
[/b] Were here to build something that lasts. Security, stability, and prosperity for both our nations. These meetings might take longer as we are still awaiting our key figures from different corporations to attend. Anything you would like to say, Mr Lundy?

[quote=montfleur;61688779][b]August 11, 2028: 3:00 AM Arrival[/b]

James Mrjkanlwyth, Lambeau, Meternisse, and Iverjkthing had no idea of what would happen when they each signed the Declaration of Grievances; however, as they stood on the platform of the newly named 5th of July station (named only that day by the crowds that had taken to the streets), the fullness of their doings washed over them

Gentlemen, we have done much since July 5th, in fact my predictions that the regime would fall in December were proven wrong, laughed Mrjkanlwyth, dressed in a full wig and waistcoat, his cane leaning lazily against his leg.

Indeed, we should be proud, but I am tinged with sadness for those who have died for the cause, intoned Lambeau.

You gentlemen speak like you are at some play, laughed Iverjkthing, It is jarring,

The king is late, mused Meternisse.

No, reports show that the train had to stop at Roselare due to the crowds that were crowding onto the tracks there, replied Lambeau.

How about the opposition, any word? asked Meternisse with a frown.

There is word that they are regrouping, Strømmism doesnt die so soon, but I have heard they are aware that the ICJ will not take too kindly to the leadership, replied James with a nod, Some intend to try to negotiate with Montfleur. 

For what? asked Lambeau.

Amnesty, 

The sound of a train soon filled the distance, and cheers from the sides of the tracks could be heard as protestors who had been waiting inside the station to avoid the humid summer heat rushed out; the once silent platform soon became a loud, echoing cacophony of hoots and clapping, and chants. 
 
It didnt take too long for the black steam engine of the royal train to pull into the station, steam throwing itself along the platforms like some sort of settling ghost, the screech of the wheels filling the air intermingling with the sounds of the crowd.

A group of news reporters rushed past towards the royal car as the first guards stepped off to prepare the ramp that would lead off the passengers, Mrjkanlwyth straightened his coat jacket, Gentlemen, he nodded, and the group began to walk slowly down the platform. 

The king brings an entourage of good report, intoned Meternisse, Apparently the heads of the parties are to be present, and the Count of Porcéan, 

I had already assumed the Count was in the city? Having made haste from Belgarde? enquired Lambeau.

Meternisse shrugged as they stopped alongside the ramp to wait for the king. 

Henri stepped off dressed in a business suit and slacks, his tie secured in place by a tie pin. Looking around, he nodded before approaching the men as the sound of, cane slamming began to cut through the crowd, cheers erupted as Henri shook hands with Meternisse and hugged Lambeau.

Gentlemen, today is the biggest day that Rosenmarkke has witnessed, now we must set the tone for the future, half-shouted Henri as the crowd and canes continued in the background.

Of course your majesty! shouted Mrjkanlwyth back, Shall we go? he asked, motioning down the platform towards the crowd.

Henri nodded as Eleonore and his guests stepped off, waving at the news cameras. The reporters tried to shout questions, but guards quickly stepped in and blocked the cameras view as the group walked down towards the crowd. 

Quite the turn-out, joked Henri to Eleonore.

Eleonore merely shook her head with a disapproving nod.

After wrangling their way through the crowd, Henri and the entourage stepped out into the station's plaza, where a smaller group of celebrations had begun to occur. Gentlemen, it is what? 3:10? asked Henri.

Yes, sir, replied Lambeau.

He nodded, Has a place for us to stay been arranged? he asked.

Yes, sir, the main delegations are expected to arrive tomorrow, replied Mrjkanlwyth.

Alright, nodded Henri, Let us go retire, we have a long day tomorrow. 

The chosen place of residence for the delegations was the House of the Misers, a large palatial complex located by the seashore of the capital that had been built in the 1780s by a local merchant and then purchased by the Rosenmarkket government in 1860 for offices, before being converted in 2006 into a hotel and sold to OrionStar hoteliers. 

The group was let into their rooms, a simple set of suits up and down the halls from each other, the king getting the historic George suite, where allegedly George IV of Llyndora had stayed in the 1820s. 

Henri, however, was not interested in sleeping, instead preparing the terms of transition that were to be discussed the following morning.

[b]6:00 AM: Morning Readiness[/b]

As the morning dawned upon Rosenmarkke, Henri, who had not slept since his arrival in the city, now sat in a conference room within the hotel, the revolutionaries on one side and Montfleurois military advisers and the heads of the Montfleurois parties on the other. 

Now that we are all here together, I am wanting to establish a sweep of the situation as it stands, my biggest concern is a messier transition than desired, as I have received already this morning reports of looting in this city, and I swear I heard gunfire coming from somewhere, began Henri.

I think it is best that we establish a clear line of communication with all organised military units to ensure and establish a chain of command, began Eleonore, The country is in shambles, and armed protestors are running around, guarding things, and so on, 

What is the situation here in the city? Asked Henri to Lambeau.

Unstable, replied Lambeau, Our informants tell us that the major government buildings are in the hands of the protestors, looting and ransacking have been undertaken, but the police were able to partially restore order.

Henri nodded firmly, Who is in control of the media right now? 

Martel stood up, Sir, that is unknown. We are working on establishing contact, 

Henri sighed, So much that we do not know, where are the experts, the leaders? 

Eleonore tapped the table, The Central Radio Building, what is its status here? she asked.

Contested, replied Martel.

Then we must go uncontest it, replied Henri, looking at the revolutionaries, Gentlemen? 

They nodded as the king rose from the table, and the rest followed, Martel ordering transport to be brought immediately, as the local guards formed an impromptu motorcade. The group got into the waiting cars, civilian vehicles, and taxis that had been hailed, and began the trip through the streets of the city.
 
Eleonore and Henri had been assigned a taxi driven by a Thývenic male Thrømm, the taxi smelled of cigarettes and the taxi driver looked like he was halfway through a hangover, nevertheless they rode on in an awkward silence that wouldve made a funeral seem loud.

Henri looked around the city, burnt out buildings, shattered windows, and crowds of people standing around dazed some fearful, some curious, the rest trudging on. Food lines had formed as the markets had been closed for several days and only forced to reopen just now, Henri frowned as the onlookers peered at the strange assortment of cars.

The CRB was a large art deco structure, built for state broadcasts in the 30s it had faithfully served as the official government communications hub, being expanded in the 70s to allow for television broadcasts as well. 

The motorcade pulled up to a hastily erected set of police blocks, Henri and Eleonore then got out. 

Milling about the entrance of the building were some revolutionaries with guns slung casually over their shoulders, some of the old regime officials who had seated themselves near the doorway, and city police, a burnt out car and several smashed windows told of the buildings existence in the past 24 hours.

Noting the arrival of the king they stood up, saluted and then approached Henri, with one of the revolutionaries, a bearded man in camo that had clearly been raided from a store, speaking first, Welcome to Tharkønn, he said bluntly.

Henri nodded, Yes, thank you, ah, we are looking to access the equipment here to produce a few orders and restore calm to the nation, is it safe? he asked looking at the building.

Safe, yes, we secured it from the government about four hours ago, it was a brutal affair, the crowd just cleared out about an hour ago, replied the revolutionary. 

Henri nodded, Good, follow me, he said before nodding for the others to follow him, walking into the foyer of the radio station as soldiers cleared the area for any hostile forces or threats to the king and his delegation.

Making their way through the halls with the help of the revolutionary, they were allowed entry into one of the radio studios which had survived the onslaught, although the blood splatter on the back wall had suggested an unfortunate happening had occurred in the past hours, however, Henri, though phased, continued on, directing the revolutionary to do his duty at the radio station.

Stepping up to the microphone, and asking Eleonore to take out her phone to begin filming a video he spoke for the first time to a waiting nation.

Fellow citizens of the revolution, 
Yesterday morning the regime finally cracked under the tremendous pressure that it had been placed under by your heroic efforts and by the efforts of the armed forces of Montfleur. The events that hace transpired in the past 24-hours, have uh, been inspiring, to say the least. But now we come to a new, uh, era, and we come to the necessary next steps in the process of unification. Firstly, the delegations from the regions of Rosenmarkke shall meet post haste to discuss the methods and plans for transition, secondly, a temporary national government shall be put into effect, with your uh, permission, of for which we are thankful for. 

All looting and rioting will not be tolerated, killing will not be tolerated, and the armed forces must be re-ordered. I command the armed forces to remain where they are, make no moves unless you hear from the uh, official radio channels which you will be informed of soon by the armed forces of Montfleur.

To the citizens of Rosenmarkke, I want to thank you for your spirit and your vigor, and I promise, we will get through this!

He nodded at the camera and stepped away from the microphone motioning for the radio broadcast to be cut.

Howd I do? he asked Eleonore.

Eleonore gave him a thumbs up, which he reciprocated, before walking out of the room to shake hands with the revolutionary. 

The first steps in a long road to recovery had been made.[/quote]

[b]7:40 AM: Meetings upon Meetings[/b]

Back at the hotel, the press had begun to gather eagerly at the doors of the lobby, wishing to catch a glimpse or even a peep from the new Rosenmarkket head of state, indeed, they were asking the questions all the citizens wished to know, yet the Council for Reunification as it had formally been named at 7:00 that morning in a press release remained elusive.

How long till the delegates arrive? asked Henri, seated at the desk in his hotel room, a pile of papers now scattered across it.

Most should arrive by noon a few by 3:00, replied Eleonore.

3:00? asked Henri, Who the hell do they think they are coming for? A dinner party?! 

Transportation has been hard since the regime fell, the trains are packed, replied Eleonore.

Alright, lets get a hold of the situation right now, what are the factions, what are our factions, etc. etc. replied Henri.

Well the regime loyalists have renewed their efforts in northern Mittlemarkke to take back some posts, these are being contested with the help of the Montfleurois troops which arrived across the border about an hour ago, the unionist faction, comprising of the gentlemen we met last-night and the delegates who are coming in at noon, are thankfully united in their goals, began Eleonore.

And what of the parties? Have you spoken wit the party leaders? Do they have any plan for reunification? Asked Henri.

Yes, they have drawn up a ten point plan that they hope to present at the luncheon today, replied Eleonore.

Excellent, do you know what it comprises of? asked Henri.

The plan mainly covers the massive economic questions, allegedly they have found a 266,000 Gilder GDP gap between the regions, inflated apparently by Thýven, which is the richest region in the country, so they are wanting to address that and other matters, replied Eleonore.

How is industry? Asked Henri.

Partially nationalised, about 25% of it I believe was nationalised and put into 24/6 shifts, replied Eleonore.

Trains?

Nationalised,

Energy?

Nationalised,

Pshaw, is there not any one piece of this nation that didnt belong to the government! exclaimed Henri in exasperation. 

Socialist economy sir, replied Eleonore.

Henri sighed, So what we need to do is create a special commission to, slowly privatise the key industries, of course we want to ensure that the prices are maintained fairly, so we bring in Montfleurois regulations to cap off any prosectors,

Of course, I am more concerned, about the men with the guns, replied Eleonore.

Yes, yes, I am also, do we have a chain of command? asked Henri.

Only the Montfleurois armed forces and those who are aware of the events of the hotel, avoiding the press isnt the best way to go about this sir, respectfully, replied Eleonore.

A good point, I want you to send a message to the pressno waitIll go down and address them, it will be, it is a firm message of unity and of dignity and of order, replied Henri rising from his seat and making haste to the door, Wish me luck, 

[b]8:10 AM The First Formal Address[/b]
The hotel staff had done their best to keep the press out, however, the press now crowded into the large lobby, where a security cordone had been set up, a makeshift podium had been dragged out and the king was coming down the staircase, cameras flashing and the clamoring voices of the press filled the air. 

Adjusting his tie Henri approached the podium, grasped the sides and spoke, I wish to address this nation, formally, and without contest, he began smiling at the news reporters, The rioting and the looting that I have heard of is barbaric and uncouth for a noble nation such as he paused as he realised Rosenmarkke technically wouldnt exist in eight hours, such as this one our beautiful nation, he continued. This is why I intend with firm resolve to settle some matters that have come up, namely the one of who is in charge, he paused, All orders and all commands are coming from this hotel, from the general Charles Martel, a great and solid man, who is currently in command of the Montfleurois armed forces. I want all militias reporting to their nearest Montfleurois army outpost to secure your weapons, and to gain cohesive commands to ensure public safety, he paused again as he shuffled the notedeck that he had made, Dear friends, soldiers and sailors, sergeants and petty officers, warrant officers and not warrant officers, officers, admirals and marshals, dear friends! I thank you for your cooperation in these affairs, I ask for your continued cooperation and your recognition of this temporary transitional government, as we traverse the waters of chaos together, the army of Rosenmarkke shall be disbanded effective immediately, all command shall be placed under Charles Martel, and all officers are to report to the headquarters of the Rosenmarkket Central Command, formally known as the Hôtel des Rousemonds, for orders and briefings over the next couple of days, thank you, 

He nodded firmly, smiled, and then returned up the stairs as the press began to clamor and shout questions over each other. Pausing at the top of the stairs the king turned, waved, and the headed back up.

[b]12:00 PM: Lunch with the revolution[/b]

The patio of the hotel facing the ocean had been prepared spectacularly for a fine luncheon, assembled around a wicker table were Lambeau, Mrjkanlwyth, and Meternisse, along with Henri who had just finished a series of phone calls with the duc of Thýven, who had informed him that he would be unable to attend the summit at 5:00 that evening. 

Well, it seems that most of our attendees will be arriving, which is good, have you the document of dissolution? Lambeau asked Henri.

Ah yes, we do, it was approved by the party leaders, replied Henri.

Alright, thats good, its certainly an emotional moment, I mean we were born here and raised here, replied Meternisse, tears welling up in his eyes, But Rosenmarkke wont truly be gone, however, the eternal revolution has reached its intended point, he smiled.

Henri patted his hand, Cheer on up, we have a few hard months ahead, and much to do, but you now have freedom and stability,

Eleonore, Dramatic as always, but who knew a group of men with wigs and canes would see this through and topple a government, she smiled.

A toast, intoned Meternisse, To freedom! 

To freedom! They all cried.

[b]6:00 PM: To dissolve a nation[/b]
[b]The Treaty of Tharkønn[/b]
In the name of the holy and undivided trinity, the representatives of the Provisional Rosenmarkket government and the Kingdom of Montfleur gathered here in the city of Tharkønn on this day of August 11, 2028 agree thus.

[i]Article I.[/i]
Where the government of Rosenmarkke having failed its duties to the people of Rosenmarkke, oppressing them unjustly and violating international law, it is therefore agreed that the government of Rosenmarkke ceased in its functions on August 10 and the provisional government under the leadership of James Mrjkanlwyth began.

[i]Article II.[/i]
It is hereby declared that the state of Rosenmarkke and its formal institutions shall cease to stand under independent jurisdiction with all powers being devolved for a period of five months to the regional authorities.

[i]Article III.[/i]
It is hereby declared that the armed forces of Rosenmarkke are hereby disbanded and released from their allegiance to the government of Rosenmarkke, with all command authority being placed under the purview of the Rosenmarkket National Salvation Front with oversight from the General Charles Martel de Funes,

[i]Article IV.[/i]
It is hereby declared that the government of Montfleur shall with all haste ensure a framework of unification is established within a week of this treaty's signing. 

[i]Article V.[/i]
All treaties, organisations, and other such foreign mechanisms by which Rosenmarkke is a member of shall be transferred into the new unified government with pending review of terms and conditions.

[i]Article VI.[/i]
The Central Bank of Rosenmarkke and its monetary authority shall be transferred over two months to the Central Bank of Montfleur with the government of Montfleur appointing a new board of governors within a month of this treaty being signed.

[i]Article VII.[/i]
Within a week of this treaty being signed the governments of Rosenmarkke and Montfleur shall meet once more to lay out the full mechanism of transfer for industry and denationalization

Signed this day August 11, 2028
